shared_elements: standing/upright anthropomorphic figure carved as a monolithic pillar
oversized head atop a columnar torso
facial features rendered as brow ridge, nose and eye
arms bent with hands brought onto the chest/abdomen
no legs shown; body tapering to a plain base
justification: Both depict the same specific subject: a monumental, legless anthropomorphic pillar-figure with a disproportionately large head above a columnar torso and arms bent so the hands meet on the chest/belly, an arrangement more particular than a generic "human figure". The main difference is that B adds a substantial incised repertoire (headdress bands, a large disc/roundel on the chest, a belt-like band, small symbolic motifs) and is conceived as a flat slab, whereas A is a plain rounded volume whose forms are modelled rather than inscribed, with no ornament or attributes at all.
